audit_findings.title: The equity-level OE anchor does not contain a full year of the acquisition debt’s interest cost
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2026 debt-interest obligation of approximately $71 million, equal to 55.0% of the $129.1 million anchor; only $9.5 million of Steelcase-transaction-related interest expense entered fiscal 2025 results
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-level OE must subtract recurring interest because debt principal is not deducted in the equity bridge; the pre-acquisition trend anchor omits most of the post-acquisition financing cost
audit_findings.evidence: Interest obligations from debt are estimated to be approximately $71 million during 2026 and $289 million thereafter.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch, not merely a possibility. HNI acquired Steelcase three weeks before fiscal year-end, while the anchor is principally derived from earlier years. A recurring interest burden of this scale is reasonably capable of materially reducing every scenario and the terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Calculate the normalized annual after-tax interest expense using the July 4, 2026 debt balances, rates, swap and debt-cost amortization; rerun all scenarios with that burden in OE without deducting debt principal again.

audit_findings.title: The earnings numerator and post-merger share denominator describe different operating perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: 25.2 million acquisition shares equal 33.6% of the 75.0848 million valuation denominator; Steelcase supplied $1,580.8 million, or 56.1%, of consolidated first-half 2026 sales
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-merger share denominator is applied to an OE anchor dominated by legacy-HNI operations and containing only three weeks of Steelcase activity
audit_findings.evidence: The year-over-year increase in shares outstanding in 2025 is primarily due to the issuance of 25.2 million shares in December 2025 as part of the consideration to acquire Steelcase.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated and quantitatively large. Adding Steelcase’s normalized operating cash generation could raise value, while adding its full interest, maintenance investment and other senior cash requirements could lower it; the supplied record does not establish the net direction.
audit_findings.action: Replace the anchor with full-perimeter normalized OE from a complete combined-company period, reconciling operating earnings, taxes, interest, maintenance capex, working capital and all diluted shares on the same basis, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Deferred cash merger consideration is a senior claim absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum disclosed acquisition-date amount of $37.6 million, equal to $0.50 per diluted share and 2.0% of the $1,922 million base equity value; the valuation-date unpaid balance is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid cash-settled award consideration for pre-acquisition service is a claim on equity value unless already included in liabilities or projected OE
audit_findings.evidence: Of the $ 864.5 million, $ 37.6 million of cash consideration represents the value of the equivalent shares for which service was provided by the grantees prior to December 10, 2025 and will be paid as the equivalent shares vest.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is demonstrated, but the remaining amount and its balance-sheet location are unresolved. Even assuming the entire original $37.6 million remained unpaid and wholly omitted, deducting it would reduce base value from $25.60 to approximately $25.10 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $49.66 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 4, 2026 vesting and payment schedule and liability roll-forward; confirm whether the unpaid balance is included in accounts payable, other liabilities or the diluted-share calculation, and deduct only any uncaptured amount.

audit_findings.title: Acquired benefit obligations may require cash beyond the expense embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed Steelcase benefit-plan liability of $146.5 million, with scheduled payments of approximately $65 million in 2026 and $82 million during 2027–2035; incremental amount not captured by OE is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Past-service pension, post-retirement and deferred-compensation cash payments can reduce equity value through OE or a bridge deduction when periodic expense does not represent the cash obligation
audit_findings.evidence: For legacy Steelcase employee benefit plans, payments are expected to be approximately $65 million during 2026 and $82 million in aggregate from 2027 through 2035.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligations and payment schedule are demonstrated, but the record does not reconcile them with benefit expense, plan assets or the $70.6 million net COLI cash-surrender value. The gross liability equals 7.6% of base equity value, so an uncaptured deficit may affect value, but materiality cannot be established without avoiding double counting.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each plan’s July 4, 2026 liability, assets, periodic expense and expected cash payments; allocate genuinely available COLI without counting borrowed or already-designated value twice, then rerun using either normalized cash expense or a net bridge deduction.

audit_findings.title: Historical capex does not represent the combined company’s recurring investment requirement
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2026 capex forecast of $130–$140 million versus $67.8 million in fiscal 2025, a $62.2–$72.2 million difference; first-half 2026 actual capex was $64.7 million; sustainable maintenance portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Understated maintenance capex inflates OE and all forecast and terminal cash flows
audit_findings.evidence: The Corporation expects capital expenditures for 2026 to be in the range of $140 million to $150 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The combined company’s current investment scale is demonstrably higher than the partial-perimeter historical amount, but the filings do not separate maintenance spending from integration, growth, technology and synergy investments. Because the disclosed difference equals 48.2%–55.9% of the $129.1 million anchor, the issue could be material, but the necessary maintenance adjustment is unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain combined-company capex by maintenance, replacement, integration, growth and capitalized software categories; normalize full-perimeter maintenance capex and rerun the valuation using that amount.

audit_findings.title: Integration costs may have been stripped despite recurring for several years
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed first-half 2026 amounts include $7.8 million of acquisition-related costs, $44.3 million of restructuring and impairment charges including cost-of-sales items, and $24.4 million of restructuring cash payments; recurring integration portion removed from OE is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back acquisition or restructuring charges that require continuing cash payments over the forecast period overstates OE and terminalizable cash generation
audit_findings.evidence: The Corporation will incur substantial expenses in connection with the integration of HNI and Steelcase.
audit_findings.explanation: Substantial continuing costs are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show the OE adjustment ledger or identify which expenditures were added back. The reported categories also contain noncash impairment, purchase accounting and unrelated restructuring, so they cannot all be treated as recurring integration cash costs. The possible valuation adjustment therefore remains materiality-uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $160.5 million latest OE calculation to every acquisition, restructuring, impairment and purchase-accounting adjustment; forecast Steelcase integration cash costs by year and rerun after retaining expected cash costs while excluding only completed or genuinely noncash items.
